quote: Men fear death, as children fear to go in the dark; and as that natural fear in children, is increased with tales, so is the other.
source: Francis Bacon, The Essays or Counsels, Civil and Moral, Of Death, the opening sentence (1625, modernised spelling)
note: Corrected: the wording is a modernised spelling text of the 1625 Essays, which is the text that was read. The 1625 quarto prints the sentence in the spelling of its day, beginning Men feare Death, so the card names the modernisation. The essay first appeared in 1612.
